characters.name: 지우
characters.note: Ji-woo, 9, Korean-American girl from Los Angeles; two short black braids, round glasses, yellow hoodie (yellow-and-pink hanbok on Chuseok).

characters.name: 할머니
characters.note: Halmeoni, Ji-woo's grandmother in a Jeonju hanok; small, silver hair in a low bun, lavender cardigan, white apron; speaks with a light Jeolla lilt.

characters.name: 엄마
characters.note: Ji-woo's mom, raised in Jeonju and now living in Los Angeles; chin-length black bob, green dress.

characters.name: 삼촌
characters.note: Uncle, Min-jun and Seo-a's father; tall and gentle, short hair, navy shirt; handles hot water and the steamer.

characters.name: 민준
characters.note: Min-jun, 11, playful Jeonju cousin; spiky black hair, blue striped T-shirt.

characters.name: 서아
characters.note: Seo-a, 6, Min-jun's little sister; pigtails, red cardigan.

scenes.title: 할머니 집 대문 앞
scenes.text: 로스앤젤레스에서 비행기를 열세 시간이나 타고, 인천공항에서 다시 버스를 세 시간 넘게 탔더니 지우의 다리는 삶은 국수처럼 흐물흐물해졌다. 아홉 살 지우에게 전주는 사진으로만 보던 도시였다. 그런데 지금 지우는 진짜로 전주 한옥마을 골목에 서 있었다. 까만 기와지붕들이 나란히 앉아 있고, 담장 위로는 빨갛게 익어 가는 감이 대롱대롱 매달려 있었다. 엄마가 낡은 나무 대문을 두드리기도 전에 안에서 슬리퍼 소리가 다다다 들려왔다. "오메, 내 새끼 왔어? 어디 보자, 이렇게 컸네잉!" 할머니가 대문을 활짝 열고 나와 지우를 꼭 안았다. 할머니한테서는 참기름 냄새와 햇볕에 말린 이불 냄새가 났다. 지우는 영상 통화로 수없이 연습한 인사를 꺼냈다. "할머니, 안녕하세요!" 할머니는 지우의 두 볼을 감싸 쥐고 활짝 웃었다. "그려, 그려. 추석이 사흘 남았응께 딱 맞춰 왔다. 올해는 우리 지우 손으로 송편도 빚어 보자." 지우는 송편을 먹어 본 적은 있어도 빚어 본 적은 없었다. 그래도 고개를 힘차게 끄덕였다. 얼마나 어렵겠어, 떡인데.
scenes.gloss_en: After thirteen hours on a plane from Los Angeles and more than three hours on a bus from Incheon Airport, Ji-woo's legs felt as floppy as boiled noodles. To nine-year-old Ji-woo, Jeonju had been a city she only saw in photos. Yet right now she was really standing in an alley of the Jeonju Hanok Village. Black tiled roofs sat side by side, and ripening red persimmons dangled over the walls. Before Mom could even knock on the old wooden gate, the pattering sound of slippers came hurrying from inside. "Oh my, is my little one here? Let me see, look how much you've grown!" Halmeoni flung the gate wide open and hugged Ji-woo tight. Halmeoni smelled like sesame oil and quilts dried in the sun. Ji-woo brought out the greeting she had practiced countless times on video calls. "Halmeoni, hello!" Halmeoni cupped Ji-woo's cheeks and beamed. "That's right, that's right. With three days left until Chuseok, you came just in time. This year, let's shape songpyeon with our Ji-woo's own hands." Ji-woo had eaten songpyeon before, though she had never made them. Still, she nodded vigorously. How hard could it be? It was just rice cake.
scenes.image_prompt: Watercolor-and-gouache children's book illustration of Ji-woo (9-year-old Korean-American girl with two short black braids, round glasses and a yellow hoodie) is hugged by Halmeoni (small silver-haired grandmother with a low bun, lavender cardigan and white apron) at an old wooden gate in a Jeonju hanok alley while Mom (cheerful woman with a chin-length black bob and a green dress) smiles beside their suitcases under a persimmon tree.

scenes.title: 사촌들과 첫인사
scenes.text: 할머니 집은 마당을 가운데 두고 방들이 ㄱ자로 둘러앉은 한옥이었다. 지우는 신발을 벗고 반질반질한 나무 마루에 올라가 보았다. 발바닥이 시원했다. 마당 한쪽에는 커다란 장독들이 뚱뚱한 형제들처럼 줄지어 서 있었다. 그때 마루 끝에서 누가 불쑥 고개를 내밀었다. 열한 살 사촌 오빠 민준이었다. 그 뒤에는 여섯 살 사촌 동생 서아가 민준의 옷자락을 잡고 숨어 있었다. "네가 미국에서 온 지우구나?" 지우는 긴장해서 침을 꿀꺽 삼키고 또박또박 말했다. "안녕! 만나서 반가워." 그런데 민준의 입꼬리가 씰룩거렸다. "방금 뭐라고 했어? 안뇽? 반가뭐?" 민준이 혀를 잔뜩 굴려 지우의 말을 따라 하자 서아가 까르르 웃었다. 지우의 귀가 뜨거워졌다. 집에서는 엄마도 아빠도 지우의 한국말을 잘한다고 칭찬했고, 토요일 한글학교 선생님은 스티커까지 주셨다. 그런 말이 여기서는 이상하게 들리는 걸까? "농담이야, 농담. 이거 먹을래?" 민준이 곶감 하나를 내밀었다. 지우는 곶감을 받아 들고 웃어 보였지만, 곶감을 씹는 동안 속으로 조금 전 그 인사를 몇 번이고 다시 말해 보았다.
scenes.gloss_en: Halmeoni's house was a hanok where the rooms sat in an L-shape around a central courtyard. Ji-woo took off her shoes and stepped onto the polished wooden maru porch. The wood felt cool under the soles of her feet. On one side of the courtyard, big earthenware crocks stood in a row like plump brothers. Just then, someone poked his head out from the end of the maru. It was her eleven-year-old older cousin Min-jun. Behind him, her six-year-old younger cousin Seo-a was hiding, clutching the hem of Min-jun's shirt. "So you're Ji-woo from America?" Nervous, Ji-woo gulped and spoke as clearly as she could. "Hello! Nice to meet you." But the corner of Min-jun's mouth twitched. "What did you just say? Hel-wo? Nice to mweet you?" When Min-jun rolled his tongue wildly to mimic Ji-woo's accent, Seo-a burst into giggles. Ji-woo's ears burned hot. At home, both Mom and Dad praised her Korean, and her Saturday Korean school teacher even gave her stickers. Did those same words sound strange here? "Just kidding, just kidding. Want one of these?" Min-jun held out a dried persimmon. Ji-woo took it and managed a smile, but while she chewed the dried persimmon, she repeated that greeting to herself over and over inside.
scenes.image_prompt: Watercolor-and-gouache children's book illustration of Ji-woo (9-year-old Korean-American girl with two short black braids, round glasses and a yellow hoodie) stands shyly on the polished wooden maru of a hanok courtyard lined with big brown crocks while cousin Min-jun (11-year-old boy with spiky black hair and a blue striped T-shirt) grins and offers a dried persimmon and little cousin Seo-a (6-year-old girl with pigtails and a red cardigan) giggles behind him.

scenes.title: 남부시장의 쌀집
scenes.text: 다음 날 아침, 할머니는 장바구니를 들고 지우의 손을 잡았다. "명절 장은 남부시장에서 봐야 제맛이여." 민준과 서아도 졸졸 따라나섰다. 전주 남부시장은 사람들 목소리와 고소한 기름 냄새로 가득했다. 밤과 대추가 산더미처럼 쌓여 있고, 어느 가게에서는 할아버지가 콩나물을 한 움큼씩 집어 봉지에 담아 주었다. 할머니는 단골 쌀집 앞에 멈춰 서서 지우의 등을 살짝 밀었다. "네가 한번 말해 볼래? 쌀가루 두 되 주세요, 하고." 지우는 숨을 들이마시고 씩씩하게 외쳤다. "아저씨, 살가루 두 되 주세요!" 쌀집 아저씨의 눈이 동그래지더니 곧 허허 웃음을 터뜨렸다. 민준은 배를 잡고 쓰러졌다. "살가루래! 살을 어떻게 가루로 만들어!" 지우는 얼굴이 빨개졌다. 쌀과 살, 지우의 귀에는 둘이 거의 똑같이 들렸다. 아저씨는 고운 쌀가루를 봉지에 담으며 다정하게 말했다. "멀리서 왔는데 이렇게 씩씩하게 말하는 게 어디여. 밤 한 줌은 덤이다." 지우는 작게 "고맙습니다." 하고 인사했다. 돌아오는 길, 장바구니는 무거웠지만 지우의 입은 꾹 닫혀 있었다. 이제 틀릴 말은 아예 하지 않기로 마음먹었기 때문이다.
scenes.gloss_en: The next morning, Halmeoni picked up her market basket and took Ji-woo's hand. "Holiday shopping only tastes right when you do it at Nambu Market." Min-jun and Seo-a tagged along right behind them. Jeonju's Nambu Market was filled with people's voices and the nutty aroma of roasting oil. Chestnuts and jujubes were piled up like mountains, and at one stall an elderly man grabbed handfuls of bean sprouts and tucked them into bags. Halmeoni stopped in front of her regular rice shop and gently nudged Ji-woo's back. "Would you like to say it? Say, 'Two doe of rice flour, please.'" Ji-woo took a deep breath and called out bravely. "Sir, two doe of flesh flour, please!" The rice-shop owner's eyes went wide before he let out a hearty laugh. Min-jun clutched his stomach and doubled over. "She said flesh flour, sal-garu, instead of rice flour, ssal-garu! How do you grind flesh into flour!" Ji-woo's face turned bright red. Ssal and sal sounded almost identical to her ears. Pouring fine rice flour into a bag, the shopkeeper spoke kindly. "Coming from so far away and speaking up so bravely is already wonderful. Here's a handful of chestnuts on the house." Ji-woo quietly said, "Thank you." On the way back, the market basket was heavy, and Ji-woo kept her mouth shut tight. She had decided she simply wouldn't say any words she might get wrong.
scenes.image_prompt: Watercolor-and-gouache children's book illustration of Ji-woo (9-year-old Korean-American girl with two short black braids, round glasses and a yellow hoodie) blushes while ordering rice flour from a smiling shopkeeper in the busy Nambu Market of Jeonju as Halmeoni (small silver-haired grandmother with a low bun, lavender cardigan and white apron) pats her back and cousin Min-jun (11-year-old boy with spiky black hair and a blue striped T-shirt) laughs beside little cousin Seo-a (6-year-old girl with pigtails and a red cardigan) among heaps of chestnuts and jujubes.

scenes.title: 솔잎 씻는 오후
scenes.text: 오후가 되자 삼촌이 커다란 소쿠리를 안고 마당으로 들어왔다. 소쿠리에는 뾰족뾰족한 초록 솔잎이 수북했다. 동네 어르신네 뒷산에서 허락을 받고 조금 얻어 온 것이라고 했다. 할머니는 수돗가에 커다란 대야를 놓고 아이들을 불렀다. "자, 솔잎 목욕 시키자. 살살 흔들어서 흙이랑 마른 잎은 골라내고." 지우는 소매를 걷고 찬물에 손을 담갔다. 솔잎을 흔들 때마다 숲속에 들어온 것 같은 향이 훅 올라왔다. "할머니, 솔잎은 왜 필요해요? 먹는 거예요?" 입을 다물기로 했던 지우였지만, 궁금한 건 참을 수가 없었다. 할머니가 웃으며 솔잎 한 가닥을 지우의 코끝에 대 주었다. "먹는 건 아니고, 떡 사이사이에 깔고 찌는 거여. 그러면 떡끼리 달라붙지 않고 솔 향도 배거든. 떡에 솔잎 자국이 콕콕 찍히면 그게 또 예쁘고." 서아는 솔잎으로 콧수염을 만들어 붙이고는 "나는 할아버지다!" 하고 뒤뚱뒤뚱 걸어 다녔다. 지우는 저도 모르게 푸하하 웃어 버렸다. 그러자 서아도 지우의 코밑에 솔잎을 붙여 주었다. 서아는 지우의 발음 같은 건 조금도 신경 쓰지 않는 것 같았다.
scenes.gloss_en: In the afternoon, Uncle came into the courtyard carrying a big woven basket in his arms. The basket was heaped high with prickly green pine needles. He said he had gotten permission to gather a little from the hill behind a neighborhood elder's house. Halmeoni set a large basin by the outdoor tap and called the children over. "Now, let's give the pine needles a bath. Shake them gently in the water and pick out the dirt and dry needles." Ji-woo rolled up her sleeves and dipped her hands into the cool water. Every time she swished the pine needles, a scent rose up as if she had stepped right into a forest. "Halmeoni, why do we need pine needles? Do we eat them?" Ji-woo had meant to keep her mouth shut, but she couldn't hold back her curiosity. Smiling, Halmeoni touched a single pine needle to the tip of Ji-woo's nose. "We don't eat them; we layer them between the rice cakes when we steam them. That way the cakes don't stick together and the pine scent sinks right in. And when the pine-needle marks press neatly into the rice cakes, that looks pretty too." Seo-a stuck pine needles under her nose like a moustache and waddled around declaring, "I'm a grandpa!" Before she knew it, Ji-woo burst out laughing. Then Seo-a stuck pine needles under Ji-woo's nose too. Seo-a didn't seem to care one bit about Ji-woo's pronunciation.
scenes.image_prompt: Watercolor-and-gouache children's book illustration of Ji-woo (9-year-old Korean-American girl with two short black braids, round glasses and a yellow hoodie) and little cousin Seo-a (6-year-old girl with pigtails and a red cardigan) wash fragrant green pine needles in a big basin at the courtyard tap, wearing silly pine-needle moustaches, while Halmeoni (small silver-haired grandmother with a low bun, lavender cardigan and white apron) watches and laughs.

scenes.title: 말 안 듣는 반죽
scenes.text: 저녁을 먹고 나서 드디어 넓은 상이 대청마루에 펼쳐졌다. 할머니는 쌀가루를 큰 그릇에 담고 삼촌을 불렀다. "뜨거운 물은 어른 일이여. 너희는 저만치 물러나 있어." 삼촌이 주전자로 뜨거운 물을 조금씩 부으면 할머니가 긴 나무 주걱으로 휘휘 저었다. 김이 모락모락 올라왔다. 반죽이 만져도 될 만큼 식자 할머니가 지우의 손을 끌어다 그릇 속에 넣어 주었다. "이제 치대 봐라. 귓불처럼 말랑해질 때까지." 지우는 자신만만하게 반죽을 꾹 눌렀다. 그 순간 반죽이 손가락 사이로 삐져나오더니 온 손에 찰싹 달라붙었다. 떼어 내려고 흔들수록 왼손에서 오른손으로, 오른손에서 안경테로 옮겨 다녔다. "으악, 얘가 나를 먹고 있어요!" 민준이 킥킥거렸다. "로스앤젤레스 반죽 괴물이다!" 이번에는 할머니도 웃음을 참지 못했다. 할머니는 지우의 손에 쌀가루를 톡톡 뿌리고, 커다란 손을 지우의 손 위에 포갰다. "힘으로 싸우지 말고, 밀고 접고, 밀고 접고. 그렇지." 한참을 치대자 거칠던 반죽이 정말로 귓불처럼 보드라워졌다. 지우는 제 귓불을 만져 보고 반죽을 다시 만져 보았다. 신기하게도 똑같았다.
scenes.gloss_en: After dinner, a wide low table was finally spread out on the main maru floor. Halmeoni poured the rice flour into a large bowl and called Uncle over. "Hot water is grown-ups' work. You children stay well back over there." As Uncle poured boiling water little by little from the kettle, Halmeoni stirred it briskly with a long wooden paddle. White steam rose in soft puffs. Once the dough cooled enough to touch, Halmeoni guided Ji-woo's hands into the bowl. "Now knead it. Until it gets as soft as an earlobe." Confidently, Ji-woo pressed down hard on the dough. That very instant, the dough squished out between her fingers and stuck fast all over her hands. The more she shook her hands to get it off, the more it traveled from her left hand to her right hand, and from her right hand onto her glasses frames. "Ack, it's eating me up!" Min-jun snickered. "It's the Los Angeles dough monster!" This time even Halmeoni couldn't hold back her laughter. Halmeoni dusted rice flour lightly over Ji-woo's hands and placed her own large hands over Ji-woo's. "Don't fight it with force—push and fold, push and fold. That's it." After they kneaded for a good while, the rough dough really did turn as soft and smooth as an earlobe. Ji-woo touched her own earlobe and then touched the dough again. Amazingly, they felt just the same.
scenes.image_prompt: Watercolor-and-gouache children's book illustration of Halmeoni (small silver-haired grandmother with a low bun, lavender cardigan and white apron) guides the flour-dusted hands of Ji-woo (9-year-old Korean-American girl with two short black braids, round glasses and a yellow hoodie), who has sticky rice dough on her glasses, at a low table on the hanok maru while Uncle (tall, gentle man with short hair, a navy shirt and oven mitts) holds a kettle safely away and cousin Min-jun (11-year-old boy with spiky black hair and a blue striped T-shirt) snickers.

scenes.title: 엄마의 어린 시절
scenes.text: 반죽을 젖은 면포로 덮어 둔 사이, 엄마가 송편 소를 준비했다. 볶은 참깨를 절구에 빻자 고소한 냄새가 온 마루로 퍼져 나갔다. 엄마는 빻은 깨에 꿀과 소금을 조금 넣고 섞은 뒤, 작은 숟가락으로 떠서 지우의 입에 넣어 주었다. 달콤하고 고소한 맛이 혀 위에서 사르르 번졌다. "우아, 이거 땅콩버터보다 맛있어!" 엄마가 푸하하 웃었다. "엄마도 네 나이 때 이 마루에서 이렇게 몰래 퍼 먹다가 할머니한테 들켰어. 그해에는 소가 모자라서 뒤에 빚은 송편은 속이 텅 비었지 뭐니." 할머니가 기다렸다는 듯 거들었다. "그려, 네 엄마는 아주 소 도둑이었어." 지우는 깔깔 웃으며 상상해 보았다. 양 갈래 머리를 한 어린 엄마가 바로 이 자리에 앉아 숟가락을 핥는 모습을. 로스앤젤레스의 엄마는 늘 바쁘게 운전을 하고 영어로 전화를 받는 사람이었다. 그런데 여기서 엄마는 말투도 웃음소리도 조금 달라졌다. 지우는 엄마 옆으로 바짝 다가앉았다. 볶은 깨, 꿀, 그리고 삶아서 으깬 밤까지, 그릇 세 개가 나란히 준비되었다. 이제 정말로 송편을 빚을 차례였다.
scenes.gloss_en: While the dough rested under a damp cotton cloth, Mom prepared the songpyeon filling. When she pounded roasted sesame seeds in a mortar, a nutty aroma drifted across the entire maru. Mom mixed a little honey and salt into the crushed sesame seeds, scooped some up with a small spoon, and popped it into Ji-woo's mouth. A sweet, toasty flavor melted across her tongue. "Whoa, this tastes even better than peanut butter!" Mom laughed out loud. "When Mom was your age, I used to sneak spoonfuls right here on this maru until Halmeoni caught me. That year we ran short on filling, so the songpyeon we shaped at the end were completely empty inside." Halmeoni chimed in right on cue. "That's right, your mom was a regular filling thief." Laughing, Ji-woo pictured a little girl with pigtails—young Mom—sitting in this very spot licking a spoon. In Los Angeles, Mom was always busy driving and answering phone calls in English. Yet here, both Mom's way of speaking and the sound of her laughter had changed a little. Ji-woo scooted right up next to her. Three bowls—roasted sesame, honey, and boiled, mashed chestnuts—were lined up side by side. Now it was truly time to shape the songpyeon.
scenes.image_prompt: Watercolor-and-gouache children's book illustration of Mom (cheerful woman with a chin-length black bob and a green dress) spoons sesame-and-honey filling into the mouth of Ji-woo (9-year-old Korean-American girl with two short black braids, round glasses and a yellow hoodie) beside a stone mortar on the hanok maru while Halmeoni (small silver-haired grandmother with a low bun, lavender cardigan and white apron) teases them both with a warm smile.

scenes.title: 감자가 된 반달
scenes.text: 할머니는 반죽을 밤톨만큼 떼어 동그랗게 굴리더니, 엄지로 가운데를 꾹 눌러 작은 그릇을 만들었다. 거기에 소를 넣고 입을 꼭꼭 오므린 다음 손끝으로 살살 눌렀다. 눈 깜짝할 사이에 매끈한 반달 하나가 상 위에 놓였다. "봤제? 요렇게 하면 되는 거여." 지우도 혀를 내밀고 집중해서 따라 했다. 그런데 소를 넣으려니 그릇이 찢어졌고, 찢어진 곳을 막으니 다른 쪽이 터졌다. 겨우 완성한 지우의 송편은 한쪽만 불룩하고 옆구리에 깨가 삐져나와 있었다. 민준이 자기 송편을 내려놓고 지우의 것을 집어 들었다. "이건 반달이 아니라 감자인데? 미국 감자!" 서아가 신이 나서 따라 했다. "미국 감자! 미국 감자!" 지우는 대꾸하려고 입을 열었다. "이건 그냥, 그냥 달이 좀 뚱뚱한 거야!" 그런데 긴장한 탓에 달이 딸처럼 나오고 말았다. 민준이 무릎을 탁 쳤다. "뚱뚱한 딸? 누구 딸인데?" 모두가 웃었다. 나쁜 뜻으로 웃는 게 아니라는 건 지우도 알았다. 하지만 지우는 더는 함께 웃을 수가 없었다. 눈앞이 뿌옇게 흐려졌고, 안경에 묻은 쌀가루 때문만은 아니었다. 지우는 조용히 일어나 마루 끝으로 걸어갔다.
scenes.gloss_en: Halmeoni pinched off a chestnut-sized piece of dough, rolled it into a ball, and pressed the center with her thumb to make a tiny cup. She spooned in the filling, pinched the rim shut tight, and pressed it gently with her fingertips. In the blink of an eye, a smooth half-moon rested on the table. "See that? This is how you do it." Sticking out the tip of her tongue in concentration, Ji-woo tried to copy her. But when she tried to put the filling in, the dough cup tore, and when she patched the tear, the other side burst open. The songpyeon Ji-woo barely managed to finish bulged on one side with sesame seeds poking out of its ribs. Min-jun set down his own songpyeon and picked up Ji-woo's. "This isn't a half-moon, it's a potato! An American potato!" Excited, Seo-a chanted along. "American potato! American potato!" Ji-woo opened her mouth to talk back. "It's just—the moon is just a little chubby!" But because she was tense, the word for moon, dal, came out sounding like ttal, daughter. Min-jun slapped his knee. "A chubby daughter? Whose daughter is she?" Everyone laughed. Ji-woo knew they weren't laughing to be mean. Even so, she couldn't laugh along anymore. Her eyes blurred, and it wasn't just because of the rice flour on her glasses. Quietly, Ji-woo stood up and walked to the edge of the maru.
scenes.image_prompt: Watercolor-and-gouache children's book illustration of Ji-woo (9-year-old Korean-American girl with two short black braids, round glasses and a yellow hoodie) holds back tears over her lumpy, split rice cake at the low table as cousin Min-jun (11-year-old boy with spiky black hair and a blue striped T-shirt) holds it up jokingly, little cousin Seo-a (6-year-old girl with pigtails and a red cardigan) giggles, and Halmeoni (small silver-haired grandmother with a low bun, lavender cardigan and white apron) shapes a perfect half-moon songpyeon nearby.

scenes.title: 마루 끝에서
scenes.text: 마루 끝에 앉아 다리를 흔들고 있으니 귀뚜라미 소리가 마당 가득 들려왔다. 잠시 후 엄마가 다가와 말없이 옆에 앉았다. 한참 뒤에 지우가 입을 열었다. 이번에는 참았던 속마음이 영어와 한국말로 뒤섞여 쏟아져 나왔다. "학교에서는 애들이 나보고 한국 애래. 도시락에 김밥 싸 가면 그게 뭐냐고 물어봐. 그런데 여기 오니까 미국 애래. 나는 대체 어디 사람이야?" 엄마는 바로 대답하지 않고 지우의 땋은 머리를 만지작거렸다. "엄마가 미국에 처음 갔을 때 말이야, 커피숍에서 물 달라는 말을 아무도 못 알아들었어. 다섯 번을 말했는데도. 그날 밤에 혼자 얼마나 울었게." 지우는 깜짝 놀라 고개를 들었다. 영어를 척척 하는 엄마한테 그런 날이 있었다니. "말이 서툴다고 그 사람이 덜 그 나라 사람이 되는 건 아니더라. 너는 두 곳의 말을 다 가진 아이야. 어렵지, 두 배로 어렵지. 그만큼 두 배로 부자이기도 하고." 지우는 코를 훌쩍였다. 금방 기분이 다 풀린 건 아니었다. 그래도 가슴을 누르던 돌멩이 하나쯤은 내려간 것 같았다. 그때 뒤에서 할머니의 목소리가 들렸다. "지우야, 이리 좀 와 봐라. 보여 줄 것이 있다."
scenes.gloss_en: As she sat on the edge of the maru swinging her legs, the chirping of crickets filled the courtyard. A moment later, Mom came over and sat down beside her without a word. After a long pause, Ji-woo spoke up. This time, the feelings she had held back came tumbling out in a tangle of English and Korean. "At school, the kids call me the Korean kid. When I pack gimbap in my lunchbox, they ask what that is. Then I come here and they call me the American kid. Where am I even from?" Instead of answering right away, Mom gently stroked Ji-woo's braids. "When Mom first went to America, nobody at the coffee shop could understand me when I asked for water. Even after I said it five times. You have no idea how much I cried by myself that night." Startled, Ji-woo looked up. To think that Mom, who spoke English so effortlessly now, had once had a day like that! "Just because your words are clumsy doesn't make you any less a person of that country. You're a child who holds the languages of two places. It's hard—twice as hard. And by that same measure, you're twice as rich." Ji-woo sniffled. Her mood didn't lift all at once. Still, it felt as though one heavy stone pressing on her chest had been set down. Just then, Halmeoni's voice called from behind them. "Ji-woo, come over here a minute. I have something to show you."
scenes.image_prompt: Watercolor-and-gouache children's book illustration of Ji-woo (9-year-old Korean-American girl with two short black braids, round glasses and a yellow hoodie) sits with dangling legs at the edge of the hanok maru under a starry autumn sky, leaning on Mom (cheerful woman with a chin-length black bob and a green dress) who gently touches her braids as lantern light glows behind them.

scenes.title: 할머니의 손자국
scenes.text: 할머니는 지우를 안방으로 데려가 서랍 깊숙한 곳에서 오래된 사진 한 장을 꺼냈다. 빛바랜 사진 속에서는 바로 이 마루에 온 식구가 둘러앉아 있었고, 앞줄에 앳된 얼굴의 젊은 여자가 쟁반을 들고 있었다. 쟁반 위 송편은 하나같이 울퉁불퉁했다. "누구예요?" "누구긴, 나지. 이 집에 시집와서 처음 빚은 것들이여. 시어머니가 이것도 떡이냐고 놀리셨다는 얘기는 네 엄마도 모를 거다." 지우가 눈을 동그랗게 떴다. 할머니도 감자를 만들던 때가 있었다니! 할머니는 지우의 손을 펴고 손바닥을 천천히 쓰다듬었다. "우리 집에서는 말이다, 송편을 찌고 나면 누가 빚었는지 다 알아맞혀. 네 삼촌 것은 크고, 네 엄마 것은 소가 적고." 할머니가 눈을 찡긋했다. "똑같이 생긴 것만 놓으면 무슨 재미가 있겄냐. 송편에는 손자국이 남는다. 그 손자국이 그 사람인 거여. 올해 상에는 처음으로 네 손자국이 올라가겄네." 지우는 제 손가락을 내려다보았다. 아직 쌀가루가 하얗게 묻어 있었다. 찌그러진 감자가 갑자기 조금 다르게 보였다. 지우는 사진을 한 번 더 들여다본 뒤 안경을 닦아 고쳐 썼다. "할머니, 저 다시 해 볼래요."
scenes.gloss_en: Halmeoni took Ji-woo into the main room and pulled an old photograph from deep inside a drawer. In the faded picture, the whole family was gathered around this very maru, and in the front row a young woman with a fresh, youthful face held a tray. Every single songpyeon on the tray was lumpy and uneven. "Who is that?" "Who else? It's me. Those were the very first ones I shaped after marrying into this house. Even your mom doesn't know that my mother-in-law teased me, asking if you could even call those rice cakes." Ji-woo's eyes went wide. Even Halmeoni had once made potatoes! Halmeoni opened Ji-woo's hand and slowly stroked her palm. "In our house, after we steam the songpyeon, we can always guess who made which one. Your uncle's are big, and your mom's have less filling." Halmeoni gave a wink. "What fun would it be if we only put out ones that looked exactly alike? Fingerprints stay on songpyeon. Those handprints are who that person is. On this year's holiday table, your handprints will go up for the very first time." Ji-woo looked down at her fingers. They were still dusted white with rice flour. All of a sudden, her lopsided potato looked a little different. After peering at the photograph one more time, Ji-woo wiped her glasses and settled them back on her nose. "Halmeoni, I want to try again."
scenes.image_prompt: Watercolor-and-gouache children's book illustration of Halmeoni (small silver-haired grandmother with a low bun, lavender cardigan and white apron) shows an old faded family photograph of her younger self holding a tray of lumpy rice cakes to Ji-woo (9-year-old Korean-American girl with two short black braids, round glasses and a yellow hoodie), gently holding her floury hand in a warm paper-windowed hanok room.

scenes.title: 라이스와 라이스
scenes.text: 지우가 마루로 돌아오자 민준이 슬쩍 눈치를 보았다. 민준의 앞에는 뭐라고 해야 할지 몰라 만지작거린 듯한 반죽 덩어리가 납작해져 있었다. "저기, 아까 그거 말이야. 그렇게까지 놀리려던 건 아니었어. 미안." 민준이 귀까지 빨개져서 웅얼거렸다. 지우는 잠시 생각하더니 입꼬리를 올렸다. "그럼 오빠 영어 잘해? 쌀이 영어로 뭐게?" "그걸 누가 몰라? 라이스!" 민준이 자신 있게 외쳤다. "다시 한번 말해 봐. 아이 러브 라이스 케이크." "아이 러브 라이스 케이크!" 지우는 그만 웃음을 터뜨렸다. "오빠, 방금 '나는 머릿니 떡을 사랑해'라고 했어. 알 소리를 엘 소리로 내면 머릿니가 된다고!" 잠깐 조용하던 마루가 와르르 무너졌다. 삼촌은 무릎을 치며 웃었고 할머니는 앞치마로 눈물을 찍어 냈다. 서아는 뜻도 모르면서 "머릿니 떡! 머릿니 떡!" 하고 뛰어다녔다. 민준은 처음에는 입을 떡 벌리고 있다가, 곧 자기 머리를 벅벅 긁는 시늉을 하며 함께 웃었다. "와, 살가루보다 머릿니 떡이 더 심하다. 인정." 지우도 민준도 서로의 얼굴을 보며 숨이 넘어가게 웃었다. 틀린 말 때문에 웃는데, 이번에는 조금도 아프지 않았다.
scenes.gloss_en: When Ji-woo returned to the maru, Min-jun glanced sideways at her uneasily. In front of him, a lump of dough he had been fidgeting with, unsure what to say, had been squashed flat. "Hey, about earlier. I didn't mean to tease you that much. I'm sorry." Min-jun mumbled, his ears turning red. Ji-woo thought for a moment, then lifted the corner of her mouth. "Then are you good at English, Oppa? How do you say rice in English?" "Who doesn't know that? Rice!" Min-jun called out confidently. "Say this after me: I love rice cake." "I love lice cake!" Ji-woo burst out laughing on the spot. "Oppa, you just said, 'I love head-lice rice cake'! If you pronounce the R sound like an L, rice turns into lice!" The maru, quiet for a second, erupted in laughter. Uncle slapped his knee laughing, and Halmeoni dabbed happy tears with her apron. Without even knowing what it meant, Seo-a ran around shouting, "Head-lice rice cake! Head-lice rice cake!" At first Min-jun sat with his mouth hanging open, and then he pretended to scratch his head furiously and laughed along. "Wow, head-lice rice cake is way worse than flesh flour. Fair enough." Looking at each other's faces, Ji-woo and Min-jun laughed until they were out of breath. Everyone was laughing over a mispronounced word, yet this time it didn't hurt one bit.
scenes.image_prompt: Watercolor-and-gouache children's book illustration of Ji-woo (9-year-old Korean-American girl with two short black braids, round glasses and a yellow hoodie) and cousin Min-jun (11-year-old boy with spiky black hair and a blue striped T-shirt) burst out laughing at the low table of half-made rice cakes while little cousin Seo-a (6-year-old girl with pigtails and a red cardigan) dances around, Uncle (tall, gentle man with short hair, a navy shirt and oven mitts) slaps his knee and Halmeoni (small silver-haired grandmother with a low bun, lavender cardigan and white apron) wipes happy tears with her apron.

scenes.title: 혀끝 수업, 손끝 수업
scenes.text: 그날 밤 마루에서는 수업이 두 개 동시에 열렸다. 하나는 민준 선생님의 발음 수업이었다. "잘 들어 봐. 달은 그냥 편하게 달. 딸은 혀를 윗니 뒤에 딱 붙였다가 숨을 꾹 참고 떼는 거야. 딸!" 지우는 손바닥을 입 앞에 대고 따라 했다. 달, 딸, 달, 딸. 숨이 손바닥에 닿으면 달이고, 거의 닿지 않으면 딸이었다. 쌀도 마찬가지였다. 그 대신 민준은 입술을 동그랗게 내밀고 '라이스'의 첫소리를 연습해야 했다. 혀가 입천장에 닿으면 안 된다고 지우가 엄하게 말하자, 민준은 강아지처럼 으르르 소리를 냈다. 다른 하나는 할머니의 손끝 수업이었다. "반죽 그릇을 너무 얇게 파지 말고, 소는 욕심내지 말고. 반달 끝은 이렇게 살짝 꼬집어." 지우의 송편은 여전히 완벽하지 않았다. 그래도 이제 터지지 않았고, 배가 조금 통통하면서도 제법 달 모양을 닮아 갔다. 서아는 콩알만 한 송편을 잔뜩 만들어 놓고 아기 달이라고 불렀다. 민준은 손가락이 굵어서인지 크기가 들쭉날쭉했다. "이것 봐, 내 건 왕감자다." 민준이 먼저 자기 것을 놀렸다. 상 위에는 어느새 크고 작은 반달들이 백 개쯤 줄지어 놓였다. 저마다 다른 얼굴로.
scenes.gloss_en: That night on the maru, two lessons took place at the same time. One was Teacher Min-jun's pronunciation class. "Listen closely. For dal, moon, just say dal comfortably. For ttal, daughter, press your tongue right behind your upper teeth, hold your breath tight, and release it. Ttal!" Holding her palm in front of her mouth, Ji-woo repeated after him. Dal, ttal, dal, ttal. If a puff of air hit her palm, it was dal; if almost no air hit it, it was ttal. Ssal, uncooked rice, worked the same way. In return, Min-jun had to round his lips and practice the first sound of "rice." When Ji-woo strictly told him that his tongue must not touch the roof of his mouth, Min-jun growled like a puppy. The other lesson was Halmeoni's fingertip class. "Don't hollow out the dough cup too thin, and don't get greedy with the filling. Pinch the tips of the half-moon gently like this." Ji-woo's songpyeon still weren't perfect. Even so, they didn't burst anymore, and though their bellies were a bit plump, they were starting to look quite like moons. Seo-a made a whole row of pea-sized songpyeon and called them baby moons. Perhaps because Min-jun had thicker fingers, his came out in all different sizes. "Look at this, mine is a king potato," Min-jun joked about his own first. Before long, about a hundred big and small half-moons were lined up across the table—each with its own face.
scenes.image_prompt: Watercolor-and-gouache children's book illustration of cousin Min-jun (11-year-old boy with spiky black hair and a blue striped T-shirt) coaches Ji-woo (9-year-old Korean-American girl with two short black braids, round glasses and a yellow hoodie) on Korean sounds with her palm held before her lips while Halmeoni (small silver-haired grandmother with a low bun, lavender cardigan and white apron) pinches a half-moon songpyeon and little cousin Seo-a (6-year-old girl with pigtails and a red cardigan) lines up tiny rice cakes on a table crowded with lopsided half-moons.

scenes.title: 솔잎 이불 덮고
scenes.text: 이튿날 아침 일찍, 부엌에는 큰 찜기가 준비되었다. 삼촌은 두꺼운 장갑을 끼고 불 앞에 섰다. "불이랑 김은 내 담당이다. 너희는 이쪽 상에서 일하고, 내가 부르기 전에는 가까이 오지 마라." 아이들 몫은 불에서 멀찍이 떨어진 상 위에서 찜기 채반을 채우는 일이었다. 지우는 어제 씻어 말린 솔잎을 한 줌 집어 채반에 폭신하게 깔았다. 서아가 그 위에 송편을 하나씩 조심조심 눕혔다. "서로 닿으면 안 돼. 잠자리가 좁으면 달라붙거든." 지우가 언니답게 일러 주자 서아가 진지하게 고개를 끄덕였다. 민준은 그 위에 다시 솔잎을 덮었다. "잘 자라, 왕감자들아." 채반이 다 차자 엄마와 삼촌이 함께 들어 찜기에 올렸다. 뚜껑이 덮이고 조금 지나자 부엌 문틈으로 김이 스며 나왔다. 어제 수돗가에서 맡았던 숲 냄새에 떡 익는 달큰한 냄새가 섞여 온 집 안을 채웠다. 아이들은 약속대로 마루에 앉아 기다렸다. 일 분이 한 시간 같았다. 지우는 코를 킁킁거리며 생각했다. 로스앤젤레스 우리 집에서는 한 번도 맡아 본 적 없는 냄새인데, 왜 이렇게 오래 알던 냄새 같을까.
scenes.gloss_en: Early the next morning, a big steamer was readied in the kitchen. Uncle put on thick mitts and stood before the stove. "Fire and steam are my job. You kids work at the table over here, and don't come near until I call you." The children's job was filling the steamer trays at a table set well away from the heat. Ji-woo grabbed a handful of the pine needles they had washed and dried the day before and spread a soft bed across the tray. One by one, Seo-a carefully laid the songpyeon down on top. "They mustn't touch each other. If their bed is too cramped, they'll stick together." When Ji-woo instructed her like a real big sister, Seo-a nodded seriously. Min-jun tucked another layer of pine needles over them. "Sleep tight, king potatoes." Once the tray was full, Mom and Uncle lifted it together and set it onto the steamer. Shortly after the lid went on, wisps of steam began seeping through the gap in the kitchen door. The forest scent from the courtyard tap yesterday mingled with the sweet, warm smell of steaming rice cakes, filling the whole house. As promised, the children sat waiting on the maru. One minute felt like an hour. Sniffing the air, Ji-woo wondered to herself: she had never smelled this at home in Los Angeles, so why did it feel like a scent she had known for a very long time?
scenes.image_prompt: Watercolor-and-gouache children's book illustration of Ji-woo (9-year-old Korean-American girl with two short black braids, round glasses and a yellow hoodie) and little cousin Seo-a (6-year-old girl with pigtails and a red cardigan) tuck rice cakes between layers of pine needles at a table far from the stove with cousin Min-jun (11-year-old boy with spiky black hair and a blue striped T-shirt) while Uncle (tall, gentle man with short hair, a navy shirt and oven mitts) in thick mitts lifts a steaming tray in the hanok kitchen with Mom (cheerful woman with a chin-length black bob and a green dress).

scenes.title: 찾았다, 내 손자국
scenes.text: 드디어 삼촌이 찜기 뚜껑을 열었다. 하얀 김이 뭉게뭉게 솟아오르자 아이들이 일제히 와 하고 소리쳤다. 어른들이 떡을 꺼내 찬물에 살짝 헹구고 솔잎을 떼어 낸 뒤 참기름을 발랐다. 커다란 쟁반에 담긴 송편은 반들반들 윤이 났고, 어제의 뽀얗던 반죽과는 전혀 다른 음식 같았다. 어떤 떡에는 솔잎 자국이 빗살처럼 곱게 찍혀 있었다. 할머니가 쟁반을 상 가운데에 놓았다. "자, 누구 것인지 맞혀 봐라." 온 식구가 머리를 맞대고 들여다보았다. 이건 삼촌 것, 저건 할머니 것, 콩알만 한 것은 물을 것도 없이 서아 것. 그때 지우의 눈에 낯익은 떡이 들어왔다. 한쪽이 불룩하고 옆구리에 작은 흉터가 있는 어제의 그 감자였다. 지우가 그것을 집어 한 입 베어 물었다. 쫀득한 떡을 지나자 소가 와르르 쏟아졌다. 깨와 꿀이 다른 떡보다 곱절은 많이 들어 있었던 것이다. "이거 진짜 맛있어!" 민준이 나머지 반쪽을 얻어먹고 눈이 커졌다. "야, 미국 감자가 제일 맛있잖아? 다음부터 나도 소 많이 넣을래." 할머니가 흐뭇하게 웃었다. "그것 봐라. 네 손자국이 벌써 한몫 단단히 하잖여." 지우는 입안 가득 떡을 물고 활짝 웃었다.
scenes.gloss_en: At last, Uncle lifted the steamer lid. As clouds of white steam billowed up, the children all cheered at once. The adults took the rice cakes out, rinsed them briefly in cold water, plucked off the pine needles, and brushed them with sesame oil. Piled on a large tray, the songpyeon gleamed with a glossy sheen, looking completely different from yesterday's pale dough. Some of the cakes had delicate pine-needle marks pressed into them like comb patterns. Halmeoni set the tray in the middle of the table. "Now, guess whose is whose." The whole family put their heads together to look. This one was Uncle's, that one was Halmeoni's, and the pea-sized ones were unmistakably Seo-a's. Just then, a familiar rice cake caught Ji-woo's eye. It was yesterday's potato, bulging on one side with a tiny scar on its flank. Ji-woo picked it up and took a bite. Past the chewy rice cake, the filling spilled right out. It had twice as much sesame and honey inside as any other cake. "This is seriously delicious!" Min-jun got the other half and his eyes went wide. "Hey, the American potato tastes the best! Next time I'm putting in extra filling too." Halmeoni smiled contentedly. "See that? Your handprint is already more than pulling its weight." With her cheeks full of rice cake, Ji-woo beamed.
scenes.image_prompt: Watercolor-and-gouache children's book illustration of Ji-woo (9-year-old Korean-American girl with two short black braids, round glasses and a yellow hoodie) takes a delighted bite of her lumpy songpyeon spilling sesame filling as cousin Min-jun (11-year-old boy with spiky black hair and a blue striped T-shirt) tastes the other half, while Halmeoni (small silver-haired grandmother with a low bun, lavender cardigan and white apron), Uncle (tall, gentle man with short hair, a navy shirt and oven mitts), Mom (cheerful woman with a chin-length black bob and a green dress) and little cousin Seo-a (6-year-old girl with pigtails and a red cardigan) gather around a tray of glossy half-moons on the maru.

scenes.title: 추석날 아침
scenes.text: 추석날 아침, 지우는 엄마가 꺼내 준 노랑 저고리와 분홍 치마를 입었다. 할머니 집 대청에는 온 가족이 모였고, 상 위에는 햇과일과 나물, 그리고 온 식구가 함께 빚은 송편이 올라갔다. 할머니는 조상님들께 올리는 차례상을 차리며 작은 접시에 송편을 하나하나 쌓았다. 맨 위 언저리에 조금 찌그러진 반달 하나가 놓였다. 지우의 것이었다. 지우는 어른들을 따라 조심스럽게 절을 했다. 할머니가 사진 속 어른들을 가리키며 이름을 하나씩 알려 주었다. 그 사람들도 이 마루에서 송편을 빚었을 것이다. 울퉁불퉁한 것도, 예쁜 것도. 지우는 처음으로 그 사람들이 멀게 느껴지지 않았다. 차례를 마친 뒤 할머니가 떡 한 접시를 건넸다. "옆집 어르신께 갖다 드리고 와. 네가 인사도 하고." 지우와 민준은 골목을 따라 옆집 문을 두드렸다. 지우는 혀끝을 준비했다. "안녕하세요, 할머니 심부름 왔어요. 쌀로 빚은 송편이에요. 추석 잘 보내세요!" 쌀이 쌀로 나왔다! 옆집 할아버지가 눈을 가늘게 뜨고 웃었다. "뉘 집 손주가 이렇게 인사를 잘 혀?" 민준이 얼른 대답했다. "제 사촌 동생이에요. 로스앤젤레스에서 왔는데, 저희 집 애예요." 지우는 그 말이 떡보다 더 달게 느껴졌다.
scenes.gloss_en: On Chuseok morning, Ji-woo put on the yellow jeogori jacket and pink chima skirt Mom had laid out for her. The whole family gathered in the main hall of Halmeoni's house, where fresh autumn fruit, seasoned vegetables, and the songpyeon the family had shaped together were set on the table. Preparing the ancestral charye table, Halmeoni stacked songpyeon one by one onto a small plate. Right near the very top rested a slightly lopsided half-moon. It was Ji-woo's. Following the adults, Ji-woo bowed carefully. Halmeoni pointed to the elders in the family photos and told Ji-woo each of their names. Those people must have shaped songpyeon on this maru too—both lumpy ones and pretty ones. For the first time, they didn't feel distant to Ji-woo. After the memorial rite ended, Halmeoni handed her a plate of rice cakes. "Take these over to the elder next door. And give him your greeting too." Ji-woo and Min-jun walked down the alley and knocked on the neighbor's gate. Ji-woo readied the tip of her tongue. "Hello, I came on an errand for Halmeoni. These are songpyeon made with rice, ssal. Happy Chuseok!" Ssal had come out as ssal! The grandfather next door crinkled his eyes and smiled. "Whose grandchild gives such a fine greeting?" Min-jun answered right away. "She's my younger cousin. She came from Los Angeles, and she's one of our family's kids." To Ji-woo, those words tasted even sweeter than the rice cake.
scenes.image_prompt: Watercolor-and-gouache children's book illustration of Ji-woo (9-year-old Korean-American girl with two short black braids, round glasses and a yellow-and-pink hanbok) proudly hands a plate of songpyeon to a smiling elderly neighbor at a tiled hanok gate beside cousin Min-jun (11-year-old boy with spiky black hair and a blue striped T-shirt) in a Jeonju alley on a bright Chuseok morning.

scenes.title: 보름달 아래에서
scenes.text: 저녁이 되자 온 식구가 돗자리를 들고 한옥마을 가까이 오목대 언덕으로 올라갔다. 전주의 기와지붕들이 까만 물결처럼 내려다보였고, 그 위로 쟁반같이 둥근 보름달이 천천히 떠올랐다. 서아가 하늘을 가리켰다. "언니, 저거 내 아기 달이 다 컸어!" 모두가 웃었다. 할머니가 도시락에서 송편을 꺼내 나누어 주며 지우에게 작은 통 하나를 쥐여 주었다. 안에는 참깨 소와 잘 말린 솔잎이 들어 있었다. "로스앤젤레스 가서도 빚어 봐라. 반달은 원래 차오르는 달이여. 네 말도, 네 손도 앞으로 계속 차오를 것이니께." 지우는 통을 꼭 끌어안았다. 이제 누가 어디 사람이냐고 물으면 뭐라고 할지 알 것 같았다. 로스앤젤레스 사람이고, 전주 할머니 집 사람이라고. 김밥 도시락도, 이 찌그러진 송편도 다 자기 것이라고. 민준이 달을 보며 진지하게 입을 동그랗게 모았다. "아이 러브 라이스 케이크." 이번에는 제법 그럴듯했다. 지우가 엄지를 들어 올렸다. 그러고는 숨을 고른 뒤 보름달을 향해 또박또박 말했다. "할머니, 달이 정말 예뻐요." 할머니가 지우의 어깨를 끌어안았다. 달은 달로, 지우의 목소리 그대로, 전주의 밤하늘로 올라갔다.
scenes.gloss_en: When evening came, the whole family carried straw mats up to Omokdae hill near the Hanok Village. The tiled roofs of Jeonju stretched out below them like dark waves, and above them a full moon as round as a tray rose slowly into the sky. Seo-a pointed up at the heavens. "Unni, look—my baby moon grew all the way up!" Everyone laughed. As Halmeoni passed around songpyeon from a lunchbox, she pressed a small container into Ji-woo's hands. Inside were roasted sesame filling and well-dried pine needles. "Try shaping them when you go back to Los Angeles too. A half-moon is a moon on its way to becoming full. Both your words and your hands will keep filling out from here on." Ji-woo hugged the container tight. Now she knew what she would say if anyone asked where she was from. That she was from Los Angeles, and from Halmeoni's house in Jeonju. That both her gimbap lunchbox and this lopsided songpyeon were hers. Looking up at the moon, Min-jun seriously rounded his lips. "I love rice cake." This time it sounded pretty convincing. Ji-woo gave him a thumbs-up. Then, after steadying her breath, she spoke clearly toward the full moon. "Halmeoni, the moon, dal, is really pretty." Halmeoni wrapped an arm around Ji-woo's shoulders. Dal rose as dal, in Ji-woo's own voice, high into the Jeonju night sky.
